# Virtual List

Use @zeus-web/virtual as a headless, one-axis virtualization foundation for large lists and higher-level Zeus Web components.

### Source

Choose the framework entry that matches your application.

::: code-group

```html [Web Component]
<script type="module">
  import '@zeus-web/virtual/wc/auto'

  const list = document.querySelector('#activity-list')
  const rows = document.querySelector('#activity-rows')

  list.addEventListener('range-change', event => {
    rows.innerHTML = ''
    event.detail.items.forEach(item => {
      const row = document.createElement('div')
      row.textContent = `Activity ${item.index + 1}`
      row.style.position = 'absolute'
      row.style.transform = `translateY(${item.start}px)`
      row.style.height = `${item.size}px`
      rows.appendChild(row)
    })
  })
</script>

<zw-virtual-list
  id="activity-list"
  count="1000"
  estimate-size="40"
  overscan="4"
>
  <div id="activity-rows"></div>
</zw-virtual-list>

<style>
  #activity-list [data-slot='virtual-list-viewport'] {
    position: relative;
    height: 20rem;
    overflow: auto;
  }
  #activity-list [data-slot='virtual-list-items'],
  #activity-rows {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
  }
</style>
```

```tsx [React]
import { useState } from 'react'
import { VirtualList } from '@zeus-web/virtual/react'

interface VirtualItem {
  index: number
  key: string
  start: number
  size: number
}

export function ActivityList() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<VirtualItem[]>([])

  return (
    <>
      <style>{`
        .activity-list [data-slot='virtual-list-viewport'] {
          position: relative;
          height: 20rem;
          overflow: auto;
        }
        .activity-list [data-slot='virtual-list-items'] {
          position: absolute;
          inset: 0;
        }
      `}</style>
      <VirtualList
        className="activity-list"
        count={1000}
        estimateSize={40}
        overscan={4}
        onRangeChange={event => {
          setItems(event.detail.items as VirtualItem[])
        }}
      >
        {items.map(item => (
          <div
            key={item.key}
            style={{
              position: 'absolute',
              transform: `translateY(${item.start}px)`,
              height: item.size,
            }}
          >
            Activity {item.index + 1}
          </div>
        ))}
      </VirtualList>
    </>
  )
}
```

```vue [Vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { VirtualList } from '@zeus-web/virtual/vue'
import { ref } from 'vue'

interface VirtualItem {
  index: number
  key: string
  start: number
  size: number
}

interface VirtualRangeDetail {
  items: unknown
  range: unknown
  scrollOffset: unknown
  viewportSize: unknown
}

const items = ref<VirtualItem[]>([])

function isVirtualItem(value: unknown): value is VirtualItem {
  return (
    typeof value === 'object' &&
    value !== null &&
    'index' in value &&
    typeof value.index === 'number' &&
    'key' in value &&
    typeof value.key === 'string' &&
    'start' in value &&
    typeof value.start === 'number' &&
    'size' in value &&
    typeof value.size === 'number'
  )
}

function updateRange(event: CustomEvent<VirtualRangeDetail>): void {
  items.value = Array.isArray(event.detail.items)
    ? event.detail.items.filter(isVirtualItem)
    : []
}
</script>

<template>
  <VirtualList
    class="activity-list"
    :count="1000"
    :estimate-size="40"
    :overscan="4"
    @range-change="updateRange"
  >
    <div
      v-for="item in items"
      :key="item.key"
      :style="{
        position: 'absolute',
        transform: `translateY(${item.start}px)`,
        height: `${item.size}px`,
      }"
    >
      Activity {{ item.index + 1 }}
    </div>
  </VirtualList>
</template>

<style scoped>
:deep(.activity-list [data-slot='virtual-list-viewport']) {
  position: relative;
  height: 20rem;
  overflow: auto;
}

:deep(.activity-list [data-slot='virtual-list-items']) {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
}
</style>
```

## When to use

- Render large activity feeds, logs, timelines or other one-dimensional collections without mounting every item.
- Build a higher-level advanced component that needs reusable range calculation, size measurement and scroll alignment.
- Support vertical or horizontal virtual scrolling with explicit overscan and imperative navigation.

## When not to use

- Do not treat this package as a model request library.
- Do not expect zw-virtual-list to render item content; the application owns the item renderer.
- Do not use it for small collections where rendering every item is simpler and inexpensive.
- Do not use the one-axis list as a substitute for @zeus-web/data-grid when rows and columns both need virtualization.
- Do not put network requests, credentials or provider-specific transport inside the virtualizer.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @zeus-web/virtual
```

## Examples

### Core virtualizer usage

Use the framework-independent engine when building a higher-level component.

```ts
import { createVirtualizer } from '@zeus-web/virtual'

const virtualizer = createVirtualizer({
  count: 10_000,
  estimateSize: 40,
  overscan: 4,
})

const range = virtualizer.getRange(0, 320)
const visibleItems = virtualizer.getItems(range)
const middleOffset = virtualizer.getOffsetForIndex(5_000, {
  align: 'center',
  viewportSize: 320,
})
```

### Native Web Component usage

Listen for range changes and render only the items supplied by the headless list.

```ts
import '@zeus-web/virtual/wc/auto'

const list = document.querySelector('zw-virtual-list')
const itemLayer = document.querySelector('#virtual-items')

list.addEventListener('range-change', event => {
  const elements = event.detail.items.map(item => {
    const element = document.createElement('div')
    element.textContent = `Activity ${item.index + 1}`
    element.style.position = 'absolute'
    element.style.transform = `translateY(${item.start}px)`
    element.style.height = `${item.size}px`
    return element
  })

  itemLayer.replaceChildren(...elements)
})

list.scrollToIndex(5_000, 'center')
```

### React wrapper usage

Use the generated wrapper and keep visible items in application state.

```tsx
import type { VirtualItem } from '@zeus-web/virtual'
import { VirtualList } from '@zeus-web/virtual/react'
import { useState } from 'react'

export function ActivityList() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<VirtualItem[]>([])

  return (
    <VirtualList
      count={10_000}
      estimateSize={40}
      overscan={4}
      onRangeChange={event => setItems(event.detail.items)}
    >
      {items.map(item => (
        <div
          key={item.key}
          style={{
            position: 'absolute',
            transform: `translateY(${item.start}px)`,
            height: item.size,
          }}
        >
          Activity {item.index + 1}
        </div>
      ))}
    </VirtualList>
  )
}
```

## AI usage hints

- zw-virtual-list is headless and does not render item nodes; handle range-change or call getItems() to obtain the current virtual items.
- Render only the returned items and position each item from its start and size values.
- Give the viewport a bounded size and overflow so the component can measure a useful visible range.
- Use scrollToIndex with start, center or end alignment for imperative navigation.
- Use createVirtualizer directly when implementing a higher-level Zeus Web component.
- Keep business request logic in the application layer.
